findings.title: Object identity comparison of two dayjs objects is always false
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, the branch `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two distinct dayjs object instances with `===`, which is always false. This check was presumably meant to detect a full-day blocked override (start equal to end), but it can never trigger, so that case silently falls through to the subsequent isBefore/isSame/isAfter checks. Use `.isSame()` instead.

findings.title: Working-hours check uses the same value for slot start and end, ignoring event length
findings.body: In the new working-hours guard inside checkIfIsAvailable, both `start` and `end` are computed identically as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`. The `end` should be the slot's end time (start + eventLength). As written, a slot that starts inside working hours but ends past the working-hours end (e.g. a 60-min slot starting 30 min before the end of availability) is treated as within working hours, so the fixed-host filter will not remove it — exactly the kind of over-booking this PR is trying to prevent.

findings.title: Slot time compared in UTC against working hours defined in organizer's timezone
findings.body: `slotStartTime` is `time.utc()`, and the new check computes `slotStartTime.hour()`/`.day()` in UTC, then compares them against `workingHour.startTime`/`endTime`, which are minutes-since-midnight in the organizer's (schedule) timezone. For any organizer not on UTC the comparison is shifted by their offset (e.g. an IST host's 9:30 start becomes 570, but a 9:30 IST slot is hour 4 in UTC), so slots will be incorrectly rejected or accepted for fixed hosts depending on timezone. The slot time should be converted to the organizer's timezone (organizerTimeZone is already passed in) before extracting hour/day.

findings.title: Override start/end minute computation wraps across midnight instead of producing out-of-range minutes
findings.body: The new override mapping computes `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 + ...minute()`. Because `.hour()` wraps into 0-23, an override whose adjusted time crosses midnight (e.g. organizer override 22:00-23:00 with invitee offset +3h becomes 25:00, reported as 1:00) produces a startTime/endTime in the wrong part of the day rather than minutes > 1440 or < 0 that the range logic could handle or clip. Overrides near midnight for invitees in distant timezones will show slots at completely wrong times. Compute total minutes from the shifted time (e.g. diff against start of day) instead of hour()/minute().

findings.title: dateOverrideExist flag makes a slot available whenever any override matches its day, even if slot is outside all overrides
findings.body: When `dateOverrides.find(...)` runs, the callback returns true only for slots outside the matching override, which correctly leads to `return false`. But if the slot's day matches an override and none of the 'outside' conditions trigger, the find returns undefined and execution falls to `if (dateOverrideExist) return true` — bypassing the busy-time check entirely. A fixed host with a date override on that day who also has a conflicting booking or calendar busy time during the override window will be reported available, allowing double bookings. The busy check should still run for slots inside an override.
